brief.headline: Apollo’s £5.7bn easyJet takeover expected to close early next year
bullets: M&A & Buyouts: Apollo Global Management’s proposed £5.7bn acquisition of EasyJet remains on course to complete in early 2027, according a report by Bloomberg citing comments from the airline’s chief executive, Kenton Jarvis, although regulatory approval is still outstanding.

AI & Technology: Unrealised losses in private credit have been a headwind to total returns, with recent markdowns concentrated in software, but these reflect uncertainty over AI rather than weakening fundamentals, according to BlackRock.
People & Leadership: In other moves, custody and clearing firm Innovayte and RIA Arax name new COOs, and Mesirow hires an investment expert from Morningstar.

M&A & Buyouts: Carlyle Group’s agreement to acquire most of Russian oil producer Lukoil’s international assets has expired, with the US private equity firm confirming it is no longer actively pursuing the transaction, according to a report by Bloomberg.

Exits & Secondaries: Blackstone has raised approximately $1bn for a private credit continuation vehicle, enabling existing investors to exit while the investment firm retains exposure to the underlying loan portfolio, according to a report by Bloomberg.
brief.marketRead: The S&P 500 stands at 7,811.54 (up 0.6% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 15.4, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.22% (down 6 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.44 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.15%, near long-run norms (up 6 bps on the prior reading). Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits.

items.title: SEC Proposes Expanding Securities Eligible for Cross Trading by Registered Funds
items.takeaway: The Securities and Exchange Commission today proposed amendments to the Investment Company Act “cross-trading rule,” which permits transactions in securities between a registered fund and its affiliates under certain conditions.
items.whyItMatters: Regulatory scrutiny of private funds is rising as the industry grows; new rules often reshape fees, disclosure and access. For allocators: new rules can change fees, transparency and eligibility, so check with advisers how they affect existing commitments.
